question: Where can I get the areas designated to protect sensitive species in Spain, such as bird protection zones for power lines or species recovery plan areas, as geometry, with species and legal effect?

answer.summary: MITECO publishes a national download (April 2026) of the bird protection zones for high-voltage lines (RD 1432/2008) as geometry, but one dissolved polygon per region, with no species or legal act. Species-level recovery-plan and critical areas, with species and legal act, exist only as regional services: Aragon is best (area critica, ambito de plan, BOA link); Andalucia, Murcia, Galicia and Navarra also publish them. No national layer of recovery areas found.
main_caveats: MITECO layer is dissolved: one multipolygon per region (Comunidad, Superficie in ha). It cannot say which species or act created a zone.
The zip named geojson contains two GeoPackage files, not GeoJSON; Canarias is a separate file in EPSG:32628, the rest EPSG:25830.
Recovery plan areas are designated by regions, not the State; coverage, species and legal fields differ per region and there is no national recovery-area layer.
Legal effect is mostly technical: RD 1432/2008 imposes line-design measures inside zonas de protección; área crítica effects come from Ley 42/2007 art. 59 and regional plans.

Madrid, Castilla-La Mancha, Cataluna and Extremadura: no layer found; Ceuta's zones are its ZEPAs; Melilla has none; La Rioja was blocked (HTTP 403 to automated clients). Pais Vasco's shapefile is lines, not zones.
answer.confidence_reason: National layer and eleven regional services tested directly; four regions had no layer found after two attempts and La Rioja was blocked.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sL -o geojson.zip 'https://www.miteco.gob.es/content/dam/miteco/es/biodiversidad/servicios/banco-datos-naturaleza/zpa/ZZPP_Abril2026_geojson.zip' ; python3 -I -c "import zipfile,sqlite3; zipfile.ZipFile('geojson.zip').extractall('gj'); c=sqlite3.connect('gj/ZZPP_Abril2026_geojson/ZZPP_2026_P.gpkg'); print(c.execute('select Comunidad,Superficie from zzpp_2026_p limit 2').fetchall())"
how_to_use.example_result: [('Andalucía', 4710495), ('Aragón', 2873461)]; peninsula file zzpp_2026_p: 18 features, EPSG:25830; Canarias file zzpp_2026_c: 1 feature ('Islas Canarias', 1443844), EPSG:32628
steps: Download ZZPP_Abril2026_shp.zip (31.6 MB) or the geojson-named zip (34 MB, holds ZZPP_2026_P.gpkg and ZZPP_2026_C.gpkg).
Open both files: P is Peninsula and Baleares (EPSG:25830), C is Canarias (EPSG:32628); reproject before merging.
Filter by Comunidad to get a region; there is no species, act or date column.
For species and legal act go to the regional services (source 2) or the regional resolutions listed in source 3.
reading_traps: The file called geojson contains GeoPackage, not GeoJSON.
Each region is a single dissolved multipolygon (18+1 features in total): individual zones, species and legal acts cannot be separated.
Layer fields documented in the dictionary: only Comunidad and Superficie. Superficie is hectares but Shape_Area is square metres.
Region sums differ slightly from regional layers (CyL 5,030,515 ha here vs 5,036,674 ha in the IDECyL service).

steps: Aragon: WFS 2.0.0 at https://idearagon.aragon.es/geoserver/ows with typeNames VISOR2D:ACRIT (areas criticas) or VISOR2D:APPE (ambito de aplicacion); use outputFormat=application/json and srsName=EPSG:4326.

Andalucia: WFS at https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/medioambiente/mapwms/REDIAM_WFS_Ayudas_Aves with typeNames ms:aves_esteparias_plan_recuperacion, ms:aves_necrofagas_plan_recuperacion, ms:aguila_imperial_plan_recuperacion or ms:aves_humedales_plan_recuperacion; outputFormat=geojson, CRS EPSG:3042.
Navarra: download the shapefile zips listed in the member; Valencia: WFS typename ProteccionLLEE.AreasPrioritarias (gpkg or GML); CyL: WFS shape-zip.
Join the legal act: Aragon legalfoundationdocument (BOA link), Valencia leg_link; for other regions use the resolution in source 3.

Galicia: ArcGIS REST MapServer layers 2-9 (query ... f=json); Murcia: WFS 2.0.0 typeNames SIG_ZOR_PLANIGEST_CARM:<layer>; Cantabria: OGC API items of collection 60; Canarias: shapefile zip; Baleares: ArcGIS REST layers 4 and 5.

Regions with no layer found (Madrid, Castilla-La Mancha, Cataluna, Extremadura, Ceuta) and La Rioja (blocked): use the MITECO national layer (source 1) for geometry and the resolution of source 3 for the act.
reading_traps: Aragon APPE and ACRIT include flora and a crayfish (Austropotamobius pallipes), not only birds; some descripcio texts say 'Ambito de proteccion' vs 'Ambito de aplicacion'.
Aragon ACRIT 144 features are parts per species (56 for the crayfish): count of areas is not count of species.
Andalucia layers come from the PRTR grant service (Orden de 21 diciembre 2023): they are the plan areas used as protection zones for line-adaptation aid, not the plan annexes themselves.
Andalucia coordinates are EPSG:3042, Navarra and Valencia EPSG:25830; CyL metadata field list does not match the service fields.

Pais Vasco: the downloadable shapefile is lines, not zones; Cantabria collection 47 is a different layer; the Baleares collision layer (4) returned a row whose TEXT says 'electrocució' (CLASE 3): check CLASE before use.
Murcia and Galicia put the species in the layer name, not in a field; Canarias species are only on the linked BOC page.

problems: Valencia WFS rejects outputformat=application/json (HTTP 400); GML and gpkg work
La Rioja pages (larioja.org, IDERioja) answer HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge to curl and to the fetch tool; IDEEX Extremadura answers a Cloudflare challenge to curl

how_to_use.example_result: Resolution text (pages 1-3) lists plans 'Águila Imperial Ibérica (Aquila adalberti), Águila perdicera (Aquila fasciata), Buitre negro (Aegypius monachus) y Grulla (Grus grus)' and says zones use UTM 1 km squares, huso 30 ETRS89, shp on the Consejería web (link dead). Annex (page 4, DOE p. 25033) is one map image titled 'MAPA DE ZONAS DE PROTECCION PARA LA AVIFAUNA EN LA COMUNIDAD AUTONOMA DE EXTREMADURA' with a legend of four plans and ten species.
steps: Open the MITECO status table and pick the region row; open the resolution link.
Read the resolution text for plans and species; the annex of this example is a map image (render with pdftoppm -png -r 130 -f 4 -l 4), not a table or UTM-square list.
Use art. 4 and 5 of RD 1432/2008 for effect: lines with bare conductors inside zones must meet the technical rules; Ley 42/2007 art. 59 for áreas críticas.
reading_traps: MITECO page does not separate columns in text: first link per region is the zones, second the list of non-compliant lines.
Extremadura resolution says shp on the Consejería web; http://extremambiente.gobex.es did not respond and the juntaex cartography page lists only ZEPA and zonings.
The annex legend lists species not named in the body text (for example Águila culebrera, Circaetus gallicus); the map is a picture, so boundaries cannot be extracted from the PDF.

evidence.quote: En las áreas críticas, y en las áreas de potencial reintroducción o expansión de estos taxones o poblaciones definidas como tales en los planes de recuperación, se fijarán medidas de conservación e instrumentos de gestión, específicos para estas áreas o integrados en otros planes, que eviten las afecciones negativas para las especies que hayan motivado la designación de esas áreas.

recipe: Open the MITECO status table and note the resolution for each region.
Open the resolution (example: DOE 2014) and read which plans and species are included; the annex there is a map image with a legend, so it gives species but not coordinates.
